evidence.V1: Stacked four-tier conifer with pointed tip and wavy skirts reads instantly as a pine from front, three-quarter and top (star-shaped wavy rings).
evidence.V2: Clear: big = four diminishing tiers, medium = light-green rim bands with wavy edge, small = capped tip; only the trunk level is missing.
evidence.V3: Tier taper is confident and stylised, but the trunk is almost invisible - only a small brown disc peeks out under the bottom skirt, making the tree look like a cone stack sitting on the ground (trunk_base close-up shows only foliage).
evidence.V4: Each tier rim has a consistent chamfered lighter band that catches light; tip has a matching cap - consistent bevels.
evidence.V5: Studio and flat close-ups of the tier rim and tip are clean: smooth gradients, no pinches, seams or z-fighting.
evidence.V6: Disciplined: foliage green in 2 values (body + rim) plus a bark brown; colourways keep the same two-value scheme.
evidence.V7: 1920 tris vs tree target 2000 / ceiling 5000 - at target.
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material, smooth shading, chamfered rims and two-value hue match the kit; bark secondary is barely visible but present.
evidence.V9: Studio line correct: Anchored, Hull collision, CanTouch off, CastShadow on, Color white, SmoothPlastic, origin bottom-centre.

top_fixes: Lengthen the visible trunk (raise the lowest tier ~0.6-1 stud) so the bark secondary and a readable trunk show below the skirt
Reframe the trunk_base close-up camera - it currently renders from inside the foliage and gives no evidence
Optionally add slight per-tier rotation or droop so the stack feels less mechanically regular
